annotation.location: source root (outside the repository), beside the heightmap
annotation.verified_clean_heightmap: The annotation is a separate RGBA copy. Outside the strokes its grey matches the 16-bit heightmap to within 0.65 grey levels (p99), and no label pixels appear in land_8k_16_eroded.png.
annotation.note: Outlines by colour: yellow mountains, blue water and ice, magenta the Rift, red the Craters, green town candidates. Extents are the stroke-enclosed areas, with gaps bridged where an outline was not closed (the gap per landmark is recorded).

coordinates: Block x, z. A1 origin at 0,0; x east, z south.

status_values.built: present in the terrain as intended
status_values.partial: present but under-delivered; needs terrain work to meet its spec
status_values.planned: not in the terrain; exists only as a spec

water_values.allowed: tools may treat ground below sea level here as water
water_values.never: ground below sea level here is not water and must not be filled, classified or routed as water

landmarks.name: The Tri Peaks
landmarks.status_basis: Three summits present inside the outline; the highest reach the y200 ceiling and are clipped flat.

extent.basis: stroke-enclosed area of the annotation outline, gaps up to 24 blocks bridged, simplified to 8 blocks

landmarks.name: Mt Vessu
landmarks.status_basis: The massif's largest summit. Its top is a clipped plateau at y200 of about 0.1 km2, and a town box is drawn on it.

extent.basis: stroke-enclosed area of the annotation outline, gaps up to 32 blocks bridged, simplified to 8 blocks

landmarks.name: Mt Clay
landmarks.status_basis: A single summit south-east of Vessu, inside a closed outline.

landmarks.name: Merian
landmarks.status_basis: A smooth, flat-floored cirque at the glacier's head, ground y107-181 (median 122). It is not a closed hollow: no basin holds water inside the outline, it opens down the Glacial Tear.

extent.basis: stroke-enclosed area of the annotation outline, gaps up to 8 blocks bridged, simplified to 8 blocks

landmarks.name: Glacial Tear
landmarks.status_basis: A continuous U-shaped trough from Merian to Lake Tilpey: median depth 35 blocks, floor 141 and rim to rim 396 blocks wide, walls 16 degrees. The floor falls from y108 to y63 with no counter-slope over 0.8 blocks.

extent.basis: stroke-enclosed area of the annotation outline, gaps up to 32 blocks bridged, simplified to 8 blocks

axes.basis: least-cost path on the lowest ground inside the outline

landmarks.name: Lake Tilpey
landmarks.status_basis: A closed basin at the glacier's end: floor y51, spill y77.9. At sea level it holds 0.74 km2 of water; filled to y77 it covers 1.16 km2, which matches the drawn outline (82% overlap). Two islands.

extent.basis: stroke-enclosed area of the annotation outline, gaps up to 24 blocks bridged, simplified to 8 blocks

water_body.basis: one block below the basin spill

landmarks.name: Unnamed tarn at the head of the ravine above Peak Pond
landmarks.status_basis: A closed hollow carved at the head of the dry ravine above Peak Pond (floor y105, spill y128.3, 23 blocks deep). Missed by the annotation and so never painted: the 2026-09-14 export left it dry. Found from the air, then by a basin search. Named here only descriptively; it needs a name. It holds water only if painted: it sits above sea level.

landmarks.name: River of Shrews
landmarks.status_basis: Not a river: from its inland end the only descent is a 1,777-block trench cut along 94% of its length (up to 11.3 blocks). Left uncut; kept on file as a possible authored canal (graded course river_of_shrews_from_high_end, marked canal in data/rivers.json).

landmarks.name: The Rift
landmarks.status_basis: A branching U-shaped trench (trunk, west spur, south-west and south-east arms): floor y82-89, median depth 36-38 blocks on the main arms, rim to rim 300-380 blocks, walls ~17 degrees. The floor is a closed basin (spill y92) and lies 20 blocks above sea level, so it is a dry valley unless painted.

surface.treatment: The floor is now above sea level and visible. The earlier void/barrier treatment and the water: never policy no longer apply; the closed basin is left dry. A custom biome is still wanted.

landmarks.name: The Craters
landmarks.status_basis: Three cones inside the outline. The great cone's top is clipped flat at y200; only the eastern cone has a bowl (7 blocks deep, floor y127). The other two read as rings in the local relief but hold no crater.

extent.basis: stroke-enclosed area of the annotation outline, gaps up to 24 blocks bridged, simplified to 8 blocks

landmarks.name: Dry ravine above Peak Pond
landmarks.status_basis: Carved toward Peak Pond; its head is less than a block above the pond with a 22-29-block rise between, so it cannot carry water. A dry ravine by design. Its head is the tarn ravine_head_tarn, which drains north to the coast instead (a 7-block cut would be needed along the carve).

axes.basis: least-cost path along the most incised ground near a guide read from the local-relief map

landmarks.name: Dry ravine, Marshy Marsh toward Lake Tilpey
landmarks.status_basis: Carved from Marshy Marsh east then south toward Tilpey. Water cannot run along it without a 31.7-block cut; the marsh drains north-east instead. A dry ravine by design.

axes.basis: least-cost path along the most incised ground near a guide read from the local-relief map

landmarks.name: Marsh outflow (unnamed)
landmarks.status_basis: Marshy Marsh's real outflow, north-east to the coast: a 1.6-block notch at the rim. Redrawn 2026-09-14 in place of the dry ravine toward Tilpey. Graded and cut.

landmarks.name: Major river (unnamed): Merian to the east coast
landmarks.status_basis: Chosen by catchment: the Tilpey system drains 14.0 km2, the largest on the map, with the longest descending path (3389 blocks) and the most tributaries (8). Its trunk runs from the flank above Merian down the Glacial Tear into Lake Tilpey and out to the east coast. Graded, incised, with floodplain and terraces where it is at least 16 blocks wide.

role.note: 20-32 blocks of water up to 9 deep, set 6-8 blocks under its floodplain in the lower Glacial Tear: players cross by bridge or boat
